timecoded_text_to_speech.text: A titration is a technique used to work out the concentration of an unknown solution
when you know the concentration of another solution.
You carefully add the known solution to a sit volume of the unknown solution until the
reaction is complete.
This enables you to work out the concentration of the unknown solution.
You may need to use the indicator to signal the end of the reaction.
You can calculate the concentration of an acid or an alkaline by carrying out a titration
experiment.
In this video we are going to look at how to carry out titrations.
In the next video we will then look at the calculations to go with the experiment.
The apparatus needed for titrations looks like this.
The buffet is needed to accurately measure a certain volume of an unknown solution into
the flask.
The buffet is then used to accurately measure and add the unknown reactant to the unknown
until the reaction is complete.
The buffet can measure up to 0.05 cubic centimeters accuracy.
To carry out a titration you follow these steps.
Using the pipette add a sit volume of the unknown solution to a clean, conical flask.
You may also need to add a few drops of indicator.
Full the barit with a known solution.
Record the starting volume on the barit.
Slowly add the solution from the barit to the unknown solution in the conical flask.
You may need to saw the flask to mix or use a stir plate.
Stop adding when the reaction is complete.
The endpoint is reached.
This is where an indicator may help because there would be an appropriate color change.
Record the final volume.
Subtract the final volume from the initial reading.
This gives you the volume of the solution added.
This volume is called the titra.
For an accurate experiment, you should repeat this experiment a few times until you get
consistent values for the titra.
Depending on indicator you use will depend if the color change is gradual or sudden change.
If you are carrying out an acid alkaline titration, you may use an universal indicator which
will give you gradual color change, whereas litmus would give you a sudden color change.
Sometimes the acid may be the known solution and the alkaline unknown and other times the
alkaline, the known and the acid unknown.
So, I have carried out the titration a few times and have a consistent title value.
What do we do next?
Tatration calculations.
Now that you know how to carry out titrations, watch a second part of this video to see how
to do a titration calculation to work out the actual concentration of the unknown solution.
All you really need to remember is that titrations are used to work out the concentration of an
unknown solution when you know the concentration of another solution.
Thank you.

youtube_description:
How To Do Titrations | Chemical Calculations | Chemistry | FuseSchool

Learn how to carry out titration experiments.

In this video, you will learn what apparatus needs to be used to conduct a titration, including pipettes, burettes and conical flasks.

Titration experiments enable us to work out the exact concentration of an unknown solute, when we know the concentration of another solute. You can calculate the concentration of acids and alkalis through this method.

You may need to use an indicator to help you spot when the acid or alkali has been neutralised.

This video shows you how to carry out the experiment, and then you will also need to know how to do the calculations to actually find the concentration.
